title: Strength — Bodyweight Advanced
subtitle: Unilateral and leverage-based strength, no equipment
coaching_note: At this level, standard push-ups and squats aren't hard enough to build strength anymore — leverage and single-limb variations are how you keep loading without weights. Every exercise here has a full regression listed; use it if a rep breaks down rather than grinding out a bad one.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Big step into a lunge, drop the back knee, plant the same-side hand, rotate the other arm up.
exercises.why: Opens hips, hamstrings, and thoracic spine together before the harder single-leg and pressing work.

exercises.name: Wrist Prep
exercises.form_cue: Circles, stretches, and weight shifts on flat hands.
exercises.why: Pistol squats and archer push-ups both put unusual load through the wrist — prep it.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat (assisted or full)
exercises.form_cue: Hold a doorframe for the assisted version if needed. Standing leg goes all the way down, other leg stays straight out in front. Chest stays tall.
exercises.why: Single-leg squat strength at full depth — a genuinely hard bodyweight strength standard that a regular squat can't reach anymore.

exercises.name: Nordic Curl (partner or anchored feet)
exercises.form_cue: Kneeling, feet anchored, lower your torso forward as slowly as you can, catch yourself with your hands at the bottom if needed.
exercises.why: The single best bodyweight hamstring exercise — eccentric hamstring strength is directly tied to reduced hamstring strain risk.

exercises.name: Archer Push-up
exercises.form_cue: Hands wide, shift your weight over one arm as you lower, the other arm stays straight and just supports.
exercises.why: Shifts near-full bodyweight onto one arm — the natural progression once standard push-ups stop being challenging.

exercises.name: Pike Push-up (feet elevated)
exercises.form_cue: Feet on a chair or box, hips high, head lowers toward the floor between your hands.
exercises.why: The elevated version increases the overhead-press demand — the closest bodyweight equivalent to a heavy shoulder press.

exercises.name: Chin-up (if a bar is available)
exercises.form_cue: Full hang at the bottom, chin clears the bar, control the lowering all the way down.
exercises.why: The best bodyweight pulling exercise available — if you have a bar, don't skip it in favor of the row substitute.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Rock
exercises.form_cue: Hold the hollow body shape and rock gently back and forth on your lower back and shoulder blades without losing the shape.
exercises.why: Adds a dynamic, harder layer on top of a static hollow hold — real core control under motion.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Back shin up a wall or couch, front foot forward, tuck your tailbone under and lean into it.
exercises.why: Pistol squats load the hip flexor hard on the trailing leg — release it before you're done.

progression_notes: Once assisted pistols feel solid for 3x6, remove the doorframe assist. Once archer push-ups feel controlled, work toward a full one-arm push-up progression next.
